value.introduction: Cheryl Bratt practices pediatrics at North Seattle Pediatrics.
value.story: Bratt grew up in Seattle. After medical school in Chicago and pediatric residency in Grand Rapids, she returned to the practice her father, pediatrician Bern Alberda, helped found. She joined North Seattle Pediatrics in 2000. Her biography describes working with parents as partners as their children grow.

approach: Working with parents as their children grow

value.introduction: Linda Grim sees children and adolescents at North Seattle Pediatrics.
value.story: Grim trained in Alabama before joining North Seattle Pediatrics in 1999. She says one reason she chose pediatrics was the chance to follow families from infancy into adolescence. Beyond office visits, her biography describes speaking with PEPS parenting groups about infant sleep.

approach: Following families over time, from early development into adolescence

value.introduction: Esther Chung sees patients from infancy through adolescence at UW Medicine’s Roosevelt pediatric clinic.
value.story: Chung studied medicine and public health at Columbia before training in Oakland and Philadelphia. Alongside her Seattle clinic work, the University of Washington describes her research on childhood adversity and poverty and her role overseeing advanced patient-care rotations for senior medical students. Her UW Medicine biography also mentions cooking and reading.

approach: Working with families on children’s health and safety
